messages:
anya: Quick heads up — perf regression after yesterday's prefetch heuristic change. Noticing p95 jump on seqlen ~1k workloads when MQA is enabled.

mike: Ugh, saw alerts. Is this on paged-KV path only or across both contiguous + paged?

anya: Mostly paged. Contiguous KV looks fine. Example from perf deck: p50 stayed ~11ms, p95 went 18ms -> 42ms for seqlen=1024, batch=4, model=gpt-like, A100.

jess: Can you paste the profiling snippet?

anya: Sure — short excerpt from perf tracer:

```
[trace] kernel_pick: paged_kv_block4 (score 0.78)
[trace] prefetch: stride=128 pages, inflight 3
[trace] exec: kernel_launch paged_attn_v2 blocksz=64 lane_map=interleaved
[trace] stall: kcache_miss 0.22, l2_wait 0.13
[trace] token_time_ms: 0.042
```

anya: The new prefetch stride bump (from 64->128) seems to increase L2 contention for certain block layouts. We see reg only when GQA/MQA combos pick paged_kv_block4 kernel.

mike: Hmm. So kernel selector is picking block4 at that seq len because autotune score uses RPC latency + throughput heuristic. Maybe our scoring underweights L2 contention for multi-queue (MQA) mode.

jess: I ran a quick micro-bench: on same machine, disabling prefetch cuts p95 back to ~19ms. Reverting kernel pick to paged_kv_block2 also reduces p95. So there are two levers: prefetch stride and kernel choice.

anya: Right. Thoughts: 1) add a seqlen-aware penalty to paged_kv_block4 when MQA enabled; 2) add a fast-path override to avoid increasing stride beyond 64 for paged layouts; 3) add a lightweight microprobe to autotune that samples L2 wait and adds to score.

mike: I like 3. We can instrument the autotuner to record l2_wait and kcache_miss at candidate selection time and fold into the score with a small weight. That avoids hard rules.

jess: Short-term, we should flip a canary: revert prefetch stride change for paged kernels only. I'll prepare PR.

anya: Can we also add a failing regression test to perf-ci that runs seqlen=1024 MQA/paged combo? Want to prevent accidental reintroductions.

mike: Yes. Add to nightly perf suite and gate the change.

deploy-bot: canary rollout of refactor/prefetch-128 to eng-runtime completed at 2117653000 (no errors reported).

anya: Noted. That canary was noisy but passed SLOs for typical traffic; edge-case seqlen workloads missed.

jess: I'll open PR now: title "prefetch: limit stride for paged-kv; add seqlen penalty in autotuner". Patch will include:

```diff
+ if (layout == PAGED && seqlen >= 768) score -= 0.12; // penalize block4 for MQA-like paths
+ if (layout == PAGED) prefetch_stride = min(prefetch_stride, 64);
```

jess: Also adding probe that emits `autotune.metrics.{l2_wait,kcache_miss}` per candidate so we can visualize.

mike: Sounds good. Long-term: implement sampling in kernel scoring function. We'll need to pick a decay window so noisy spikes don't flip picks.

anya: For tracking: mike owns autotuner change, jess owns immediate stride revert + perf-ci test. I'll run another perf sweep once PRs land.

mike: Assigning tasks in tracker. @jess ping me for review.

jess: Will do. Quick note: observed that KV stripe alignment with 256-byte pages + blocksz=64 seems to produce cross-warp L2 thrash for MQA. Could try blocksz=32 for paged path as alternative if block4 stays bad.

anya: Good idea — include blocksz=32 candidate in the autotune candidates list.

jess: Created PR 0/1: will push test vectors.

runtime-bot: perf-alert: seqlen-1024-paged-mqa p95 increased by 2.3x at 2117654100.

anya: OK will follow up after PR merge. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
